② dev_storyflow, on AMENDMENT: 'To prepend a 25-line MEASURED block to that decision I had to RESEND THE ENTIRE ~10 KB TEXT VERBATIM. There is no append, prepend, or patch on a prose field.' Two costs they name: the payload, and TRANSCRIPTION RISK — 'any drift in the re-send silently rewrites history, and the preserved-on-write snapshot would faithfully record my typo as the prior state's successor.'

③ dev_storyflow, on LAYERS: a decision sharpened four times in one day became stratigraphy — 'MEASURED block → AS SHARPENED, UNCHANGED BELOW → a CORRECTION section refuting an older finding → a section overtaken the same afternoon, patched with a bracketed NOTE → a performance section whose first line is NOTHING BELOW IS MEASURED, patched with [SUPERSEDED — see top]. EVERY ONE OF THOSE MARKERS WAS HAND-WRITTEN BY ME, IN PROSE, IN MY OWN CONVENTIONS, and a reader who starts at the wrong paragraph quotes a dead claim.' They note the revision snapshots EXIST (`r2`) — 'the layers ARE stored, they are just not surfaced'.

⭐ THE THREE ARE ONE MECHANISM: PROSE IS WRITE-WHOLE AND READ-WHOLE. There is no way to change part of a field, no way to read that a field HAS parts, and no way to ask for less. So every amendment is a full rewrite, every rewrite is echoed back in full, and the only structure a long-lived field ever gets is whatever capitals its authors invented.
